items.title: Man Charged in Murder Plot Wanted Child Dead to Stop Them From Testifying
items.summary:
A man who’s in jail awaiting trial on child pornography charges is accused of trying to hire someone to kidnap and kill a child as part of a scheme to stop them from testifying in his criminal case.

Carlos Manuel Miranda-Berrios , of Kissimmee, Florida, now faces charges in connection with what the Osceola County Sheriff’s Office described as a murder-for-hire plot targeting the child — and the child’s mother if she tried to intervene.

Miranda-Berrios, 30, “had plans for the child to be abducted, subjected to heinous acts, and killed in a manner intended to cause extreme suffering,” the sheriff’s office said in a news release on Monday, November 16.

He’s charged with two counts of solicitation to commit murder, two counts of attempted murder, tampering with a victim, solicitation to commit a forcible sexual offense against a child and solicitation to commit kidnapping of a child, according to the agency.

Man Charged in Murder-for-Hire Plot Targeting Ex-Girlfriend, 2 Men 

Detectives learned Miranda-Berrios arranged for the child’s murder to prevent their court testimony in his separate case investigated by Kissimmee police, the sheriff’s office said.

He devised the alleged murder scheme while behind bars at the Osceola County Jail, where records show he’s currently detained.

Miranda-Berrios allegedly offered payment in exchange for the child’s killing and extra money to have their mother killed if she tried to get involved.

Authorities didn’t specify how much money was offered for their deaths.

items.t: Man Charged in Murder Plot Wanted Child Dead to Stop Them From Testifying

items.title: Man Allegedly Shot Sister to Death After Their Mom Died in Hospice Care
items.summary:
Police believe that a Mississippi man fatally shot his sister after their mother apparently died of natural causes while in hospice care at their home.

Richard Timothy Ward was charged with three counts of attempted murder on Monday, November 16, after he shot at three deputies with the Escambia County Sheriff’s Office in Pensacola, Florida.

Officers in Long Beach, Mississippi, also said that Ward, 64, is the prime suspect in the killing of his sister, Kimberly Hernandez . However, he has not yet been charged with her murder.

Long Beach police reported to a home on the morning of Friday, November 13, after they received a report of a shooting after a hospice worker found two dead women in the home.

Man Allegedly Shot Ex-Girlfriend's Mom, Brother to Death at Family's Home 

Hernandez, 63, and her mother, Doris Crimmins , were later identified as the victims, according to WLOX .

The coroner said that Hernandez was fatally shot, while Crimmins, 84, apparently died of natural causes while she was in hospice care. An autopsy is expected to be performed at a later date, which will determine Crimmins’ official cause of death. Both Hernandez and Crimmins lived at the home where they were found dead.

Ward was quickly named a suspect in the case and was tracked to the Sweet Dreams Inn in Pensacola, Florida, which is about 130 miles from where his mother and sister died.

Escambia County Sheriff Chip W. Simmons said in a video shared via Facebook that deputies located and approached Ward in his hotel room on Friday afternoon.

As he was approached, Ward allegedly pulled out a…

“Traditions are starting officially, kind of, now with our son because he’s now more aware of Santa and reindeer,” Lohan, 40, exclusively told Us while celebrating the launch of her Marshalls Unwrap the Internet partnership. “A tradition that we have is we always watch Rudolph together — the original old one, the old cartoon one.”

Lohan, who welcomed son Luai with husband Bader Shammas in 2023, shared that their family also reads “a lot of Christmas books” to ring in the holidays.

“Wrapping the presents is going to be the fun part,” she gushed of their tradition. “And just seeing his face on Christmas morning.”

“I always have to watch Love Actually during Christmas time,” she told Us of her go-to flick in the holiday genre. “It makes me so happy, that movie. I love The Holiday. I love Miracle on 34th Street . We always watch Home Alone . That’s my husband’s pick.”

items.title: Aaron Rodgers Calls Out Female Reporter for Being ‘Dramatic’ After Blowout Loss
items.summary:
Aaron Rodgers didn’t appreciate the line of questioning from ESPN reporter Brooke Pryor following the Pittsburgh Steelers’ blowout loss at the hands of the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday, November 15.  

During a post-game press conference after the 36-18 defeat, Pryor asked Rodgers, “How do you keep a loss like this from changing the trajectory of your season?” 

“That’s very dramatic there, Brooke,” the quarterback, 42, said with a smile. Rodgers continued, “You know, I’ve been a part of this league for a long time. There’s big wins, there’s tough losses. We’ll deal with this appropriately.” 

Pryor asked Rodgers a follow-up question about the team’s road struggles this season — they are 2-3 away from home, while a perfect 4-0 in Pittsburgh — but he was similarly disinterested.  

Lions’ Aidan Hutchinson Seen Using Wheelchair at Airport After Sack Injury 

“Yeah, I don’t know,” he said. “We’ll look at that.” 

Pryor, who has worked for ESPN since 2019, managed to have some fun with the viral interaction. She posted a clip from Rodgers’ answer via Instagram , writing, “Am I the drama?” 

Rodgers and the Steelers started remarkably slow on Sunday night, with the quarterback racking up only 27 passing yards through the first three quarters. He finished 15-for-29 passing for 143 yards and two touchdowns.  

After the game, Rodgers said he was “not happy with the way we performed on offense.” 

“Couldn’t get anything going until the fourth quarter,” he continued. “So that’s disappointing.” 

Rodgers added, “We kind of shot ourselves in the foot with a couple plays.” 

The…

A substitute teacher in Kentucky sobbed in court while admitting that she sexually abused a 16-year-old student and sent him compromising pictures over the course of their relationship.

Mary “Hanna” Mattingly pleaded guilty to first-degree sexual abuse of a minor and possession of material portraying a sexual performance by a minor during a hearing on Friday, November 13, according to WKYT .

Mattingly, 32, broke down in tears as she admitted to the crimes, which took place while she was working as a Bardstown High School substitute teacher and assistant soccer coach, per the outlet.

Her inappropriate relationship with the student began on March 1, 2025, and lasted until July 31, 2025. Mattingly’s relationship with the student began when the married teacher asked him to help her clean the girl’s locker room when she was a coach, according to statements obtained by The Courier Journal .

Teacher Shows Police Where She Had Sex With Student, 17, in Bodycam Footage 

The victim claimed that he and Mattingly would “sit down and talk about her life and what is going on.”

As their relationship progressed, they began to communicate on Snapchat “more and more.” Police also said that Mattingly sent the victim nude photos of herself over the course of their communications.

The Bardstown City Schools learned about the incident when they received an anonymous letter that “alleged inappropriate conduct between a female substitute teacher and a student,” the district previously said in a statement.

Mattingly was fired from her job in March after the district launched an…

items.title: Susan Smith's Ex-Husband David Will Oppose Her Parole: She's Not 'Remorseful'
items.summary:
More than 30 years after Susan Smith shocked the nation by drowning her two young sons, her ex-husband, David Smith , is preparing to face the parole board to keep her behind bars.

Ahead of Susan’s upcoming parole hearing on Thursday, November 19, David tells Us that he and his wife, Tiffany Smith , plan to attend and urge the board to deny her release.

Susan’s first parole hearing occurred in 2024, and the board unanimously denied her release following emotional pleas from David, Tiffany and their daughter, Savannah.

“I’m not looking forward to speaking again and going through that, but I do plan on being there every time,” David tells Us .

NC Mom Michele Hundley Smith Won't Face Charges, Left Due to 'Domestic Issues' 

David says he plans to “speak from the heart” when addressing the board, wanting to keep the focus on his late sons, Michael and Alex, who were just 3 years old and 14 months old when they were killed in 1994.

“I’m going to tell them, don’t keep her incarcerated because of what she’s done to me. Keep her incarcerated because of what she did to Michael and Alex,” David says. “Her behavior through the years [in prison] has shown it’s still all about Susan. In my heart of hearts, I don’t think she’s remorseful, and I don’t think she really cares what she did.”

Susan, now 55, was sentenced to life in prison in 1995 after rolling her car into South Carolina’s John D. Long Lake with her boys strapped inside. The case drew nationwide attention, with Susan initially claiming a man carjacked her and took the children. She famously appeared on TV with David by…

items.title: Alex Murdaugh Claims Investigator Lied About Evidence in Wife and Son’s Murders
items.summary:
Alex Murdaugh ’s lawyers are alleging that the lead investigator in his wife, Maggie Murdaugh , and their son Paul Murdaugh ’s murder case lied about evidence during his first trial,

During a Friday, November 13, pretrial hearing, Murdaugh’s attorneys and prosecutors presented their latest arguments in front of Circuit Judge Debra McCaslin while requesting the court dismiss the murder indictment against the disgraced former lawyer.

Alex’s attorneys asked the court to dismiss the indictment against him “without prejudice,” claiming that former lead State Law Enforcement Division (SLED) Investigator David Owen lied while testifying before the Colleton County grand jury in 2022, according to the ABC 11 .

items.title: I saw how brightly stars like Russell Brand could shine, but there is darkness in the shadows | Sophie Heawood
items.summary:
After years of celebrity interviews, I have learned not to be fooled by the allure of fame. We never really know them – we know what they want us to know

As I sat in Southwark crown court, listening to the final day of Russell Brand’s trial, there was one subject that came up repeatedly, invoked as often by his defence as the prosecution. I don’t mean sex or coercion, but fame. It ran through every victim impact statement and loomed so large in the courtroom that it felt as if it was almost on trial itself.

I’m an entertainment journalist who has been covering celebrities for more than 20 years – as long as Brand has been one – and I have written about him at various stages of his career. But I went to Southwark crown court as a member of the public who wanted to see justice done. For the women he had hurt, for the ones who couldn’t get as far as the courtroom, and for all of us who came of age at a time when rape culture was so fast and furious that young women mistook it for a joke that we were in on. In the age of lads’ mags, sex felt cheapened, yet somehow we were the ones who ended up paying for this. So it was doubly strange to sit in court and feel somehow complicit in it - in how this media culture had encouraged Russell Brand.

Continue reading...
items.t: I saw how brightly stars like Russell Brand could shine, but there is darkness in the shadows | Sophie Heawood

items.title: Two courtrooms, one celebrity: how did the Russell Brand case compare with the rape trial next door?

One was a high-profile defendant watched by more than 100 journalists. Another was an unknown man who preyed on a girl almost half his age. Their stories played out minutes apart, one entirely out of the spotlight

What is going on inside Russell Brand’s head as he arrives at court for the start of his rape trial? He sees the dozens of cameras and journalists lined outside Southwark crown court, many of whom have been waiting since before 7am, and he tells himself that the media are all against him. “It seems to me that they believe that I am guilty, and that this should be the rubber-stamping of the process of my destruction.”

He walks with his wife, Laura, and his bodyguard past the photographers, “clickering, clackering, snickering paparazzi, like locusts, peculiar concoctions, not fully humans”, and up into the court, where he is suddenly overwhelmed by “the presence of something very beautiful, grace”. “In a situation like I’m in, it’s impossible not to turn to God. Truth and justice are the only things that can save me,” he thinks.
